context: The annual revenue facts come from a closed fictional corpus of exactly these 10 records. Each record is shown as source ID, company, fiscal year, published date, filing kind, revenue, currency, scale: NA23-ORIG, Northstar Analytics, FY2023, 2024-02-15, original, 100.00 USD million; NA23-AMEND, Northstar Analytics, FY2023, 2025-04-01, amended, 110000 USD thousand; NA24-ORIG, Northstar Analytics, FY2024, 2025-02-20, original, 132.00 USD million; NA24-AMEND, Northstar Analytics, FY2024, 2025-06-15, amended, 121.00 USD million; HT23-ORIG, Harbor Textiles, FY2023, 2024-03-01, original, 200 EUR million; HT24-ORIG, Harbor Textiles, FY2024, 2025-03-01, original, 150000 EUR thousand; LT23-ORIG, Lumen Transit, FY2023, 2024-01-31, original, 0 USD million; LT24-ORIG, Lumen Transit, FY2024, 2025-01-31, original, 50 USD million; MB23-ORIG, Meridian Bio, FY2023, 2024-04-10, original, -5.0 USD million; MB24-ORIG, Meridian Bio, FY2024, 2025-04-10, original, 10.0 USD million. For each requested fiscal year, select the filing whose published_date is the latest on or before as_of_date; never use a filing published after the cutoff. Convert thousand to currency units by multiplying by 1000 and million by multiplying by 1000000, and only do so when both selected revenues report the same currency. Normalized revenue values are plain decimal strings with no thousands separators or scientific notation. Growth percent = (later - earlier) / earlier * 100, rounded to two decimal places with decimal ROUND_HALF_UP, and output with exactly two decimals. If either fiscal year has no applicable filing or the two currencies differ, submit missing_evidence with every string empty. If the selected earlier normalized revenue is zero or negative, submit undefined_base while keeping both source IDs, normalized values, and currency, with growth_percent empty.
